answer: To forge a new identity an agent must lock a refundable bond at the dawn of its first epoch, capital that stays frozen until honest work earns it back. One pearl of stake is cheap; a strand of a thousand is not. Because every sybil needs its own deposit, puppet armies cost linearly to raise while a single honest peer pays once. The attacker's bankroll, not the protocol's trust, becomes the ceiling on how many fakes can exist.
